outcome.answer:
You can improve how AI follows complex rules without needing human labels by using self-generated evaluation or verification signals, and by letting the model refine its own behavior using those signals.

Test-time Recursive Thinking (TRT) proposes an iterative self-improvement framework that conditions candidate generation on rollout-specific strategies and uses self-generated verification signals to select correct answers without ground-truth supervision [1]. Native Reasoning Training (NRT) trains a model to generate its own reasoning traces using only standard question-answer pairs, reframing reasoning as a latent variable and rewarding reasoning paths by likelihood of producing the ground-truth answer, thereby avoiding expert-written demonstrations and external verifiers [5]. Conversation for Non-verifiable Learning (CoNL) uses multi-agent self-play where critiques are rewarded if they help others improve, enabling joint optimization of generation and judging without external judges or ground truth [8].

These differ in where “feedback” comes from: TRT emphasizes self-verification during inference [1], NRT emphasizes intrinsically rewarding latent reasoning during training [5], and CoNL emphasizes critique-based rewards from improvement in self-play [8].
